quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Open to Feedback] Faisal told his team he wanted honest feedback on his plan. Each time someone pointed out a weakness, he explained why it would not matter. By the end of the hour, nobody was offering anything.
quests.question: What is the difference between what Faisal says and what he does?
options: He wants feedback only from managers, so he brushes aside what everyone else says.
He is probably too busy to listen to anyone.
He accepts every criticism he hears.
He says he welcomes feedback but reacts as if he does not.
quests.correctAnswer: He says he welcomes feedback but reacts as if he does not.
quests.hint: Compare what Faisal says he wants with what he does each time.
quests.explanation: His statement and his responses do not match. Explaining away every criticism discourages people, which is why they stop speaking. The team's silence is the result, not the cause.
clueWords: explained why it would not matter

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Gift Receipt] Dan's aunt gave him a sweater and a gift receipt. "Just in case," she said. "I know you're picky." Dan wore the sweater to every family lunch that winter and never went near the shop.
quests.question: What did Dan do with the sweater?
options: He exchanged it without telling his aunt.
He never liked it, but forgot the receipt.
He decided to keep it rather than exchange it.
He wore it only to make her feel bad.
quests.correctAnswer: He decided to keep it rather than exchange it.
quests.hint: Look at what he did over the winter and what he did not do.
quests.explanation: The receipt offered an easy way out, but Dan wore the sweater repeatedly and avoided the shop. That shows he chose to keep it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Approved Already] Lena said she would leave at five to miss the traffic. At 5:40 she was still at her desk, rewriting a paragraph her manager had already approved.
quests.question: Why is Lena still at her desk?
options: She is waiting for the traffic to clear.
She finds it hard to leave work she thinks could be better.
She has probably been told to stay late.
She did not understand her manager's approval.
quests.correctAnswer: She finds it hard to leave work she thinks could be better.
quests.hint: What has changed since she set her leaving time?
quests.explanation: She missed her own deadline to leave and is working on text that needs no changes. Her behaviour suggests she is unsatisfied with something others accepted.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Lucky Socks] Joon-ho wore his green socks to the three matches his team won. Yesterday he forgot them and the team lost 3–0. The coach had also moved their best defender to the bench.
quests.question: What is the best-supported explanation for the loss?
options: The other team was tired.
The team played worse because the players were tired after winning three matches in a row.
The coach wanted the team to lose.
Changing the defence probably affected the result.
quests.correctAnswer: Changing the defence probably affected the result.
quests.hint: Ask which change is connected to how a football team actually plays.
quests.explanation: Socks and wins may be coincidence, but moving the best defender changes how a team defends. The passage supports that explanation more than a superstition.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Library Quiet] Since the "Please Keep Voices Low" sign went up in the library, the noise has dropped. During the same month, exams began and many students left for home.
quests.question: What can be concluded about the sign?
options: It caused the exams to start.
It has made no difference, since the library goes quiet whenever students are busy.
It made no difference at all.
It may have helped, but the exams could also explain the quiet.
quests.correctAnswer: It may have helped, but the exams could also explain the quiet.
quests.hint: Are there other events in the same month that could produce the same result?
quests.explanation: The sign and the exams happened around the same time. The evidence does not show which caused the quiet, so the sign's effect is unproven.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Sleepless] Whenever Ilse drinks coffee after six, she sleeps badly. Last night she had only herbal tea, yet she lay awake for hours. The neighbours were having a party.
quests.question: What is the most likely explanation for last night?
options: Noise from the neighbours kept her awake.
She always sleeps badly on Thursdays.
The tea had caffeine in it.
She was worried about coffee.
quests.correctAnswer: Noise from the neighbours kept her awake.
quests.hint: What was different last night, and what else was happening?
quests.explanation: Ilse's usual cause, coffee, was absent. The passage offers another disturbance, the party, which better explains her sleeplessness.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Reading the Menu] Adaeze scans the menu, asks the waiter whether the sauce contains nuts, and reads the ingredients list twice before ordering plain rice and grilled fish.
quests.question: Why does Adaeze ask about nuts?
options: She is trying to eat as little as possible.
She has eaten at this restaurant before.
She needs to avoid nuts.
She dislikes sauces in general.
quests.correctAnswer: She needs to avoid nuts.
quests.hint: Which question does she ask, and how carefully does she check the answer?
quests.explanation: Asking specifically about nuts and rereading the ingredients show she is being careful about one item, and ordering plain food fits that.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Team Lead] Ben's manager offers him the team leader role. Ben thanks her, asks how much travel it involves, says he will "think about it," and changes the subject.
quests.question: What is Ben's most likely reaction?
options: He is delighted and only needs a day to celebrate.
He has already accepted another job.
He wants a bigger office.
He feels reluctant, probably because of the travel.
quests.correctAnswer: He feels reluctant, probably because of the travel.
quests.hint: Which question does he ask, and what does he do right after?
quests.explanation: His only question concerns travel, and his vague answer followed by a subject change is how people avoid saying no directly.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Behind the Camera] In every photo from the party, Mr. Oduya is either holding the camera or standing at the edge of the group. When his daughter calls, "Come in, Dad!" he laughs and says, "Someone has to take it."
quests.question: Why does Mr. Oduya stay out of the photos?
options: He wants to keep the pictures for himself and to control which ones are shared.
He dislikes his daughter.
He would rather stay out of the photos than be in them.
He does not enjoy the party.
quests.correctAnswer: He would rather stay out of the photos than be in them.
quests.hint: Look at where he stands, and how he answers the invitation to join.
quests.explanation: He keeps to the edge or behind the camera and gives a light excuse. That suggests he prefers not to be in the picture.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Fading Away] In September Ravi waved to everyone in the block. By December he took the stairs to avoid the lift and stopped answering knocks. A letter from the landlord lay unopened by his door.
quests.question: What is the best-supported inference?
options: He has moved out of the building.
He has started a night job.
He is withdrawing, possibly because of a problem he does not want to discuss.
He has recently moved into the building and does not yet know his neighbours' names.
quests.correctAnswer: He is withdrawing, possibly because of a problem he does not want to discuss.
quests.hint: Compare September with December, and list what he stopped doing.
quests.explanation: He shifts from friendly to avoiding people, and he ignores an important letter. That pattern suggests a problem he is avoiding.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Fewer Minutes] Until March, Emilia had never been late for training. Now she arrives after the warm-up and leaves quickly. Her coach has said nothing, but he has stopped picking her for the first team.
quests.question: What is the most reasonable connection to draw?
options: The coach has found a better player.
The coach's decision may be related to her changed attendance.
Emilia has asked to leave the team.
The coach is unhappy with her play in matches and is trying out other players.
quests.correctAnswer: The coach's decision may be related to her changed attendance.
quests.hint: Which change in behaviour happens first, and what follows?
quests.explanation: Her lateness begins first, and the coach's decision follows. The passage links them by timing, though it does not state the reason.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Clean Kitchen] Marcus usually leaves his mug in the sink. This week he has washed every cup, thrown out the old milk, and wiped the floor. His rent is due on Friday, and his landlord is visiting on Thursday.
quests.question: Why is Marcus cleaning so much?
options: The landlord asked him to get the flat ready for the next tenant.
He is planning to move out.
He wants to make a good impression on his landlord.
He has probably been asked to clean by his flatmates.
quests.correctAnswer: He wants to make a good impression on his landlord.
quests.hint: What is happening on Thursday?
quests.explanation: His new tidiness starts just before a visit, and the passage gives no other event. It fits a wish to impress.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Room 314] "Reception? It's room 314. I've been waiting since eight for the extra towels. And could you tell me whether the heating is working? It's quite chilly in here."
quests.question: What is the guest doing on the phone?
options: The guest is asking for a refund.
The guest is politely raising more than one problem.
The guest is asking about a nearby restaurant.
The guest is planning to check out.
quests.correctAnswer: The guest is politely raising more than one problem.
quests.hint: Count how many requests there are and check the tone.
quests.explanation: The guest mentions a delay and a possible heating fault while staying polite. This is a courteous complaint.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Number Fourteen] The driver checks his phone, then rings the bell again. A light comes on next door. "Looking for number 14?" a voice calls. "That's on the other side of the block."
quests.question: What was the driver's problem?
options: He did not have the right keys.
Nobody was home.
His delivery was probably too heavy.
He had come to the wrong address.
quests.correctAnswer: He had come to the wrong address.
quests.hint: Read what the neighbour says after the light comes on.
quests.explanation: The neighbour corrects the location, so the driver is at the wrong place, not at the right place with no answer.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Group Work] Every time the class does group work, Hyun ends up with all the tasks nobody else wants. Yesterday she quietly asked the teacher whether she could work alone.
quests.question: Why did Hyun ask the teacher this?
options: She feels the workload in groups is unfair to her.
She dislikes the topic.
She finds the teacher unfriendly.
She wants a higher grade than everyone else.
quests.correctAnswer: She feels the workload in groups is unfair to her.
quests.hint: What does she get "every time" in group work?
quests.explanation: The pattern of unwanted tasks builds to a request for a different arrangement. That suggests she feels the division of work is unfair.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [School Gate] The elderly man waits by the school gate at 3:15 every day. When the children come out, one girl runs over, drops her bag at his feet, and starts talking before he can say hello.
quests.question: How are the girl and the man connected?
options: He is her teacher.
They are close, and he may be a relative.
He is a stranger she has just met.
He is probably the school guard.
quests.correctAnswer: They are close, and he may be a relative.
quests.hint: Focus on how she greets him and how regularly he is there.
quests.explanation: He arrives every day, and she treats him with ease and enthusiasm. These signs suggest a close bond.
clueWords: starts talking before he can say hello

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Sign-offs] Ms. Ito ends emails to clients with "Best regards," to Ken in accounts with "Thanks, Ken," and to Hala with "thx!! see u at lunch."
quests.question: How close is Ms. Ito to Hala compared with her other contacts?
options: Ms. Ito dislikes writing emails.
Their relationship is the most casual of the three.
Hala is probably a client.
Ms. Ito is angry with Hala.
quests.correctAnswer: Their relationship is the most casual of the three.
quests.hint: Compare the three endings.
quests.explanation: The ending for clients is formal, Ken's is moderately friendly, and Hala's is slang and a lunch plan. That shows the most familiar relationship.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Letter of Reference] Professor Wells wrote three pages for Nadia's application. "She questioned almost everything I said in class," he wrote, "which is exactly why I trust her judgment."
quests.question: How does Professor Wells regard Nadia?
options: He barely knows her.
He wishes she asked fewer questions.
He respects her independent thinking.
He finds her disrespectful.
quests.correctAnswer: He respects her independent thinking.
quests.hint: What does he say the questioning proves?
quests.explanation: He treats her questioning as evidence of good judgment, which is a compliment.
clueWords: exactly why I trust her judgment

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [One Word] Hye-won's reply to the group chat was a single word: "Sure." Usually she sends paragraphs, jokes, and a string of emojis.
quests.question: What might Hye-won's one-word reply mean?
options: She has lost her phone.
She has become more talkative.
She may be upset or distracted this time.
She agrees strongly with the plan.
quests.correctAnswer: She may be upset or distracted this time.
quests.hint: Compare this reply with her usual messages.
quests.explanation: The single word stands out against her normal style. Inferring how she feels depends on that contrast.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Sealed Letter] Kwabena kept the letter in his pocket all day, touching it now and then. When he finally opened it, he read it standing up, sat down heavily on the steps, and began to laugh.
quests.question: What was probably in the letter?
options: It contained a bill he could not pay.
It contained good news that relieved him.
It was probably a joke from a friend.
It was addressed to someone else.
quests.correctAnswer: It contained good news that relieved him.
quests.hint: What does his behaviour change from carrying to reading to laughing suggest?
quests.explanation: Keeping it unopened suggests he was worried. Sitting heavily suggests a release of tension, and laughing shows the news was good.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Public Praise] When her manager thanked her in front of the team, Selin thanked her back quickly and began shuffling her papers. Later that afternoon she reread the manager's follow-up email three times.
quests.question: How does Selin most likely feel?
options: Indifferent to the praise.
Worried she will be blamed later.
Annoyed at being interrupted.
Pleased, but uncomfortable being praised in public.
quests.correctAnswer: Pleased, but uncomfortable being praised in public.
quests.hint: Compare her public reaction with her private one.
quests.explanation: Shuffling papers shows discomfort in front of others, while rereading the email shows the praise mattered to her.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Closing Times] The museum shop closes thirty minutes after the museum. The museum closes at 5:30. Beatrix arrives at 5:45 and finds the shop door open.
quests.question: What can she infer?
options: The shop will stay open for about fifteen more minutes.
The shop stays open all night.
The museum is still open.
The shop closed at 5:30 with the museum, so the open door is a mistake by the staff.
quests.correctAnswer: The shop will stay open for about fifteen more minutes.
quests.hint: Combine the two facts before comparing with her arrival time.
quests.explanation: The museum closes at 5:30, so the shop closes at 6:00. She arrives at 5:45, so about fifteen minutes remain.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [If It Rains] "If it rains on Saturday, we'll do the museum," says Aaliyah. "If not, the beach." On Saturday morning she packs towels and sunscreen.
quests.question: What was the weather on Saturday morning?
options: It was not raining.
It could not be judged from the passage.
It was raining heavily.
It was snowing.
quests.correctAnswer: It was not raining.
quests.hint: Match what she packs to the plan she stated.
quests.explanation: Towels and sunscreen belong to the beach plan. Her plan for the beach applied only if it was not raining.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Email Chain] "Please send the report by Friday." "Will do." [Monday] "Any update?" "Apologies, I'm finishing it now."
quests.question: What does the second exchange reveal about the report?
options: The report was cancelled.
The report was sent on time.
The report was rejected by the reader.
The report was late.
quests.correctAnswer: The report was late.
quests.hint: What day is it when the second message is sent?
quests.explanation: The deadline was Friday, but the follow-up on Monday shows it was still unfinished. The reply, "Apologies," adds to the impression of lateness.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Waiting for Mr. Cole] "Is Mr. Cole in?" "He's in a meeting." "I can wait." "It may be a while. He has another meeting after this one, and then he's leaving for the airport."
quests.question: What is the receptionist really suggesting?
options: That Mr. Cole is at the airport now.
That waiting is unlikely to lead to a meeting.
That Mr. Cole will make time for the visitor if he waits until the afternoon.
That the visitor should come tomorrow.
quests.correctAnswer: That waiting is unlikely to lead to a meeting.
quests.hint: Add up the events listed after "It may be a while."
quests.explanation: By listing meetings and an airport trip, the receptionist politely warns that there is little chance of a conversation today.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Confidence] "You've certainly got a lot of confidence," Ms. Ferro said, looking at the design, "to present this without testing it."
quests.question: What is Ms. Ferro really saying?
options: She disapproves of presenting an untested design.
She is offering to test it.
She wants to present it herself.
She admires the design's beauty.
quests.correctAnswer: She disapproves of presenting an untested design.
quests.hint: Read the compliment together with what follows "to."
quests.explanation: The words sound like praise, but the last part identifies the problem. She is criticising the lack of testing.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Ordering] "Are you ready to order?" "Give us a few more minutes," says Alec. His friend hasn't opened her menu. She has been watching the door for ten minutes.
quests.question: Why is the friend watching the door?
options: They are waiting for someone else to join them.
They have already ordered and are waiting for the waiter to bring the food.
The menu is probably in a foreign language.
Alec does not want to eat.
quests.correctAnswer: They are waiting for someone else to join them.
quests.hint: Whose behaviour explains the delay?
quests.explanation: The friend is not reading the menu and keeps checking the door, which suggests another person is expected.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [New Layout] The app changed its layout on Tuesday. On Thursday its help page added a short video titled "Finding your saved items."
quests.question: Why might the help page have added the video?
options: Saved items were removed from the app.
The video was made months in advance.
Users had asked the company to introduce a new video guide to explain the app.
Users were having trouble finding their saved items after the change.
quests.correctAnswer: Users were having trouble finding their saved items after the change.
quests.hint: What might make a company add a help video two days after a change?
quests.explanation: A help video appearing shortly after a change suggests the change created confusion. The title points to saved items in particular.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Shorter Menu] The café's chalkboard used to list eleven sandwiches. Now it lists four, and each has a new price.
quests.question: What might the café have decided?
options: To simplify its menu.
To close down soon.
To hire more staff.
To lower every price.
quests.correctAnswer: To simplify its menu.
quests.hint: What happened to the number of items, and what stayed the same?
quests.explanation: Cutting items from eleven to four suggests simplification. Nothing supports closing or hiring.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Cover Letter] Nomvula's cover letter never mentions her last job. Instead it describes a volunteer project in detail, then says she is "keen to return to full-time work."
quests.question: What does Nomvula's letter suggest about her recent work history?
options: She has never worked before.
She was recently promoted.
She has been out of full-time work for some time.
She has left the volunteer project.
quests.correctAnswer: She has been out of full-time work for some time.
quests.hint: Which phrase suggests she is coming back to something?
quests.explanation: "Return to full-time work" implies she is not in it now. Focusing on volunteering rather than her last job suggests a gap.
